spans.content: That in the following year 1780 he was again called out twice the first time in June and marched to fort Ann and Lake George under the command of Capt Yates was employed in scouting parties and guarding the country served as a sergeant and was in actual service two weeks. The second time in this year that this deponent was called out was in the fore part of the fall and marched to Fort Edward and Whitehall under the command of Capt Yates, served as a sergeant and was in actual service at this time two weeks employed in watching the enemy and guarding the country;. That in 1781 this deponent was called out and served under captain yates and Major Groesbeck in May marched to Palmertown to guard that place and the adjoining country was in actual service at this time and served as a sergeant three weeks was then discharged and sent home. That in the following October this deponent entered the service again and was called out by Capt Yates, John Van Antwerp Ensign and marched to Palmertown Saratoga country and was employed in helping a garrison at that place and in scouting the country was employed as a sergeant and in actual service at this time two weeks and was then discharged and sent home. That in the following year 1782 and in the fore part of the summer this deponent was again called out under Captain Yates and marched to Otsego under the command of General Clinton in pursuit of the hostile Indians was in actual service at this time three weeks when he was discharged and sent home. That in the fall of this same year this deponent was again called out by Capt Yates & John Van Antwerp Ensign and the last of September or the first of October and marched to Jessups Patent and in Saratoga County N. York went out on a scouting party to watch the enemy and was in actual service at this time as a sergeant one week was then discharged and sent home. And this deponent further says that he was born in 1760 Albany County N. York lived there about ten years then moved to Schaghticoke Rensselaer Co. N. York where he resided about twelve days when he moved to then Cambridge Washington Co. N. York but now Hoosick Rensselaer N. York where he still resides—has a record of his age—never received a written discharge from the service and this deponent further says that during the several periods of service above mentioned he was not employed in any civil pursuit. (Signed with his mark) Wynant Vandenburgh Sworn before me on this 12th day of July 1833. H. Knickerbacker first Judge of Rensselaer County. Letter in folder dated September 7, 1933, written in response to an inquiry. Reference is made to your letter in which you request the Revolutionary War record of Wynant C. Vandenburgh. The data furnished herein were obtained from the papers on file in pension claim, S.32032, based upon the Revolutionary War service of Wynant C. Vandenburgh.
